title: Split control-plane demarcation and fallback notes
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and sketches for a hybrid split-controlplane topology: demarcation of responsibilities between regional leaders and a lightweight global coordinator, plus routing/fallback semantics for DR and partial faults. This is a working page — rough, prioritized for engineers planning the POC and failure-injection tests.

Summary / high-level idea
---
- Avoid a single monolithic control-plane leader for all regions. Instead, use a two-tier model: regional leaders (full control-plane authority for region-local decisions) + global coordinator (metadata, ownership, cross-region routing policies).
- Two operating modes considered: 1) loose active-active (regions independently accept leadership for local workloads, global coordinator is advisory), 2) controlled active-passive (global coordinator delegates primary to one region but can reassign). We suggest a hybrid: default active-active for reads and local config, plus explicit global arbitration for cross-region state (billing, quotas, global rollouts).

Why this direction (short rationale)
---
- Latency: local leader handles fast path (routing, lease grants, prefix cache invalidation) to keep SLOs low.
- Availability: regional autonomy means regional outage doesn't take entire product offline.
- Complexity tradeoff: we accept additional coordination surface for global invariants rather than a hard global consensus that increases failover coupling.

Sketch (ASCII)
---
Global clients -> edge proxies -> regional routers -> region control-plane (leader)
                          
        [Global Coordinator] -- async metadata sync --> [Regional Leader A]
                                 
                              [Regional Leader B]

- Regional leaders own per-region topology, node assignment, and fast routing changes.
- Global coordinator owns policy records, rollout manifests, and conflict resolution hooks.

Demarcation of responsibilities (proposed)
---
- Regional leader (strong responsibilities):
  - Instance assignment and health-driven evictions in-region
  - Short-lived leases and fast leader arbitration within the region
  - Cache invalidation for KV-prefix caches used by runtime
  - Serving-side routing decisions (which backend pool for a tenant)
  - Local metrics ingestion and alerting thresholds (region-specific)

- Global coordinator (weaker/slower responsibilities):
  - Global policy (quota pools, price tiers, cross-region routing preferences)
  - Model catalog authoritative mapping (global model ID -> allowed region variants)
  - Rollout orchestration: staged global rollouts and canary policies
  - Cross-region failover orchestration and manual DR commands

Leader election patterns and lease sizing
---
- Regional leader election: keep simple RAFT-like lease within region, but optimize for short failover (target 5-10s detection + handover). Example lease TTLs: 15s lease, heartbeat 3s, failover backoff 30s.
- Global coordinator leadership: single logical leader per control plane (small quorum across regions). Election can be slower (30–90s) because operations are non-latency-critical. Use explicit fencing tokens for global operations.

Routing & client affinity semantics
---
- Default client routing: prefer home-region affinity (via geo-DNS, EDNS-client-subnet, or proxied region hints).
- Session stickiness: token-level preferred-region stamped in tokens for up to 24h. If region is unavailable, fall back to nearest healthy region.
- Consistency for model versions: model pins travel with token. If a pinned model is unavailable in fallback region, fall back to compatible variant (defined in model-catalog).

Failure modes & fallback behaviors (runbook outline)
---
1) Region partial outage (control-plane degraded):
   - Edge proxies will retain routing rules cached for up to 60s.
   - If leader eviction occurs, regional leader election triggers and a standby region may be promoted for tenants with cross-region failover enabled.
   - Automatic fallback: client requests are routed to region B if region A fails 3 consecutive health probes (30s).

2) Global coordinator unreachable (regional leaders healthy):
   - Regions continue serving local traffic using last-known global policy (stale) for up to 6 hours for non-security-critical fields.
   - Any global-only operation (billing adjustment, global rollout changes) is queued locally and reconciled when global coordinator returns.

3) Split-brain risk during network partition:
   - Use lease fencing and monotonic operation IDs for global operations.
   - In ambiguous cases, prefer read-only or degraded mode until manual reconcile. Avoid automatic rollback of global data without quorum.

Operational controls and knobs
---
- Grace windows: allow cached configs to be honored for T_cache (default 60s), then degrade to fallback routing.
- Promotion policy: tenants opt into auto-promote to standby region on fail; defaults to manual for high-compliance tenants.
- Throttles: when region is in degraded mode, reduce burst capacity (scale tokens) by configured factor to protect cold start strain on fallback regions.

Testing matrix (what to inject)
---
- Control-plane leader loss (kill leader process) — measure time to new leader + routing convergence
- Network partition between a region and global coordinator — verify queued ops do not diverge
- Model-catalog divergence — simulate version missing in fallback and assert expected fallback model chosen
- Canary rollback during partial outage — ensure safe rollback policy does not cause mass cascades

Decision matrix (quick)
---
- If latency-first tenant and regulatory locality required -> regional leader + pin, no auto-promote.
- If high-availability tenant and cross-region allowed -> auto-promote with quota reservation in standby region.
- If cost-sensitive -> route to cheapest healthy region (respecting data residency labels).

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (notes-to-self)
---
- How much logic should be pushed into edge proxies vs regional leaders? (pros: faster; cons: more proxy complexity and harder to standardize)
- TTLs for stale global policy: 6 hours feels long; maybe make per-policy TTLs.
- Can we do global coordinator as a passive stream consumer (no writes) to reduce danger of split-brain?
- How to surface fallbacks to application teams (SDK hooks / response headers / telemetry)?

Runbook excerpt for on-call (quick actions)
---
- Symptom: "region X leader flapping"
  1) Check leader logs (tenant-metrics) and last heartbeat (region/leader/heartbeat metric)
  2) If election thrash > 3 in 5m, force failover to standby leader after investigation ticket created
  3) Notify product owners for tenants impacted by pinned-region policies

Telemetry & SLOs to add
---
- Regional control-plane latency (median + p99) for leader ops
- Time-to-reroute: measure time from health degradation to edge routing change propagated
- Stale-policy-window: count of requests served with policy older than N minutes
- Cross-region failover success rate and cold-start CPU spike metric

Implementation notes / quick API sketches
---
- Control-plane API: GET /policy/{tenant} returns {policyId, policyVersion, recommendedRegions[], stampedAt}
- Lease API: POST /region/{r}/lease -> {leaseId, expiresAt, leaderId}
- Promotion API: POST /failover/promote -> {tenant, targetRegion, dryRun=true}

Jira/PR checklist for the prototype
---
- INF-2120: prototype regional leader election + lease semantics
- INF-2185: edge-proxy caching + fallback header instrumentation
- PR: increase model-catalog tolerance for missing variants (lib-models#57)

Notes for reviewers
---

- Please comment inline with realistic constraints: infra cost, operational burden, and compliance boundaries.
